newsitem.title: FRANCE: North Korea wants aid but no prying journalists.
newsitem.headline: North Korea wants aid but no prying journalists.

text.p: The head of Communist North Korea's diplomatic mission to France said on Friday that his country needed up to 2.4 million tonnes in food aid from developed nations to prevent its people -- now getting 100 grams of food a day -- from starving.
But it did not want prying Western journalists to witness the famine or to see how aid was distributed, Pak Dong Tchoun, also his country's ambassador to UNESCO, told a news conference.

Pak repeatedly scolded a journalist from the French Communist daily L'Humanite, once unswervingly loyal to fraternal parties, for reporting a Japanese media allegation that some foreign aid to North Korea had been re-exported for hard cash.
"The state of health of our population is very bad since the average daily intake of food has dropped from 700 grams a day to just under 100 grams," Pak said.
"We greatly appreciate the food aid the world has given to us and which amounts to between 600,000 and 800,000 tonnes.
"Unfortunately, because there is now a drought, following several years of catastrophic floods, we need twice or three times that much aid before October when we have our harvest," he said.

Appealing to foreign media to highlight the plight of his population, Pak said his country was "extremely reticent" about opening its doors to the Western press "which says it is equitable but writes horrible calumnies about our regime the minute they leave the country.

"The Korean people do not want to receive journalists who have bad intentions. We want journalists who show good will and want to promote friendship between peoples, not subvert our regime and sovereignty," he said.
"We do not want shortcomings reported. The (Western) mass media must not write articles that are not encouraging," he said.
Foreign journalists present, and who had not heard such comments since long before the fall of the Berlin Wall, were even more surprised when Pak lashed out at the Humanite correspondent.

"How can a Communist newspaper repeat such things?" Pak said about a report in the Japanese press which spoke of cereals given as aid to North Korea being re-exported to Japan for cash via China. He denied the report.
The French journalist retorted that the Paris mission gave no information about the situation despite repeated requests from his newspaper which wanted to appeal to its readers to help.

"We have a magnificent food distribution system," said Pak who assured his listeners North Korea would bring "no change whatsoever to our Socialist system which is the best for the Korean people. We will change nothing in agriculture, nothing in industry, nothing," he said.
